# ViAir On Board Air System Installation

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Install a ViAir On Board Air System by mounting components, wiring them, and connecting hoses. [t991]

[Partial] Mount an ARB CKMA12 compressor, run fused power from the battery to a switch with six buttons, then invert it near headlights. [t272]

[Partial] Mount the air tank and connect custom-length 1/4-inch hoses with swivel fittings between the compressor and the tank. [t440]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the back cargo area cover and wet storage compartment.
2. Line up the air tank and compressor to mark holes on the underside of the truck.
3. Drill eight holes total, four for the tank and four for the compressor.
4. Mount the compressor in its marked position.
5. Mount the tank in its marked position.
6. [Partial] Run all necessary wiring from components to the dash switch.
7. Connect the pressure switch wires according to their markings on the tank mount.
8. Attach the rest of the hoses and lines to the tank assembly.
9. Hook up the pressure relief valve and draincock connections.
10. Drill a hole in the bumper large enough for the 3 foot air hose.
11. Connect the female quick connect fitting into the new bumper hole.
12. [Partial] Apply Teflon tape to all tank connections and any other air line fittings.
13. Mount the dash panel where desired on the interior.
14. Connect the air line from the pressure gauge to the dash panel.
15. Hook up the wire running from the switch to a power source.
16. [Partial] Attach the ground wire for the ViAir dash switch to the rear relay location.
17. Check all hoses and lines for any leaks.

_Procedure reported by [t991]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-viair-on-board-air-system.2717/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t272] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Mount the compressor near the battery or in a location with easy access.
2. [Partial] Run power from the battery to an inline fuse, then connect that fused line to a switch.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t440] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Mount the air tank in a convenient location such as under the rear seat, on the driver's side plastic panel, or beneath where the spare tire used to sit.
2. [Partial] Connect custom-length 1/4-inch hoses with swivel fittings between the compressor and the tank if standard barbed fittings leak.

</details>

## Tips & gotchas

- Keep the compressor close to the tank because the braided line is short. [t991]
- Be careful when running the air line to the gauge as it kinks easily. [t991]
- [Partial] Consider relocating the compressor to near the headlight for cooler temperatures if using a front bumper mount. [t272]
- [Partial] Invert the unit so the air intake faces up to prevent mud and debris accumulation. [t272]
- Use Loctite 545 over Teflon tape on fittings as suggested by Viair. [t440]
- Order custom-fit hoses that have permanent, crimped-on swivel fittings for better sealing. [t440]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Using standard barbed hose clamps which may leak under pressure. [t440]
